Back to Guard
Guard

Audit, detection, compliance

Track API usage, monitor configurations, and detect threats.

1. Core Concept

  • Visibility is required for security. You must know who made an API call (CloudTrail), how a resource was configured (Config), and if active threats exist (GuardDuty).

2. Key Services & Features

  • CloudTrail:
    • Records 'Who did What, When, and from Where'.
    • Management events are free for 90 days.
    • Data events (like S3 object reads) cost extra and must be explicitly enabled.
  • AWS Config:
    • Records point-in-time configuration state of resources.
    • Evaluates compliance against rules.
    • Can trigger auto-remediation via Systems Manager (SSM).
  • GuardDuty:
    • Intelligent threat detection.
    • Uses machine learning to analyze CloudTrail, DNS, and VPC Flow Logs.
    • Requires zero architecture changes or agents.
  • Amazon Inspector:
    • Scans EC2, Lambda, and ECR for software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and network exposure.
  • Macie:
    • Uses ML to discover sensitive data (PII) specifically in S3 buckets.

3. Architecture Rules

  • Send Organization CloudTrail logs to a central, restricted S3 bucket in a separate logging account.
  • Use EventBridge to capture GuardDuty findings and trigger automated isolation workflows via Lambda.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • You need to prove to auditors exactly who deleted a production EC2 instance.
    • Choose: CloudTrail.
    • Why: It is the only service that tracks user identity for API actions.
  • You need to automatically revert any Security Group that opens port 22 to the world.
    • Choose: AWS Config with SSM Auto-remediation.
    • Why: Config detects the state change, and remediation executes the fix.

Q58 According to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which of the following is AWS's responsibility?
  • A Encryption of data at rest in S3
  • B Patch management of guest operating systems on EC2
  • C Physical security of data centers
  • D Configuration of security groups
Answer: C

- AWS is responsible for "Security OF the Cloud" - physical infrastructure - This includes data centers, hardware, and facilities - Customers are responsible for "Security IN the Cloud" - Options A, B, and D are all customer responsibilities - Customers choose whether to encrypt, patch OS, and configure security

Open isolated question ↗
Q59 A company has regulatory requirements to ensure that data stored in AWS does not leave a specific geographic location. How can this be achieved?
  • A Enable AWS GuardDuty
  • B Choose the appropriate AWS Region and do not enable cross-region features
  • C Use AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies
  • D Enable AWS CloudTrail
Answer: B

- Data in an AWS Region stays in that Region unless you explicitly configure otherwise - No cross-region replication, backups, or data transfer ensures data residency - GuardDuty is for threat detection, not data residency - SCPs can enforce policies but the key is choosing the right Region - CloudTrail is for logging, not data residency - Primary control: select Region and don't configure cross-region services
